verdict.rationale: AFK's own marketing claims encrypted secrets and scoped OAuth tokens for its connected tools (Mercury, Gusto, Carta, Stripe), which suggests central credential storage. It also claims shared company context and role-based access controls across a team. It never says credentials themselves are shared with teammates or that access can be restricted per credential, and the only evidence is landing-page copy. Missing for 10: explicit team sharing of connection credentials, per-credential permission controls, in-depth docs on credential management, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: Scoped OAuth tokens, encrypted secrets, automatic key rotation, and full audit logs.
Shared company context across your team. Role-based access controls, delegated approvals
Query and act across Mercury, Gusto, Carta, Stripe, and more from a single surface.
